q01:
We are ahead of pace to date, but if nothing changes the program lands at 57329 doors on Election Day, 3303 short of the 60632 goal.
- Program: 33503 doors to date vs a goal to date of 32431, 103.3% of pace; projected 57329, -3303 vs goal (94.6% of goal) [table:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 112.5% of pace, projected 23583, +908 vs its 22675 goal (104%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Harbor: 105.3% of pace, projected 19150, -1007 vs its 20157 goal (95%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Eastgate: 89.3% of pace, projected 14596, -3204 vs its 17800 goal (82%) [table:v_office_pace]
- Projection = doors to date plus the last 7 days' average daily doors (1489.1 program-wide) times the 16 knocking days left [doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]

- Harbor: 11.1 needed vs 9.9, so 1.3 extra [table:v_office_pace]
- Northside: 10.1 needed vs 11.1, so 0 extra [table:v_office_pace]

q05:
Ask the client for more doors: at our current pace we will knock more doors than the untouched turf we have left, and new turf beats a second pass.
- Capacity for the rest of the program: 23826 doors (1489.1 a day times 16 days left) [table:v_office_pace]
- Untouched doors left in our turf: 10393 program-wide (Eastgate 1183, Harbor 8096, Northside 1114) [table:v_turf_summary]
- By office, capacity tops untouched turf in Eastgate (6091 vs 1183) and Northside (9936 vs 1114); Harbor still has more untouched doors than capacity (8096 vs 7798), so it keeps working its own turf [table:v_office_pace] [table:v_turf_summary]
- Even so the program projects 57329 doors, -3303 vs goal [table:v_office_pace]
- Rule: when capacity is larger than untouched doors, ask for more doors first; a second pass on the 18555 not-home doors is the fallback because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate [doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass] [table:v_turf_summary]

q09:

q13:
QC is getting better program-wide, down to 3.4 flags per 100 shifts this week from 4.3 last week; Harbor and Northside improved, while Eastgate got worse.
- All offices: 8.1, 6.1, 4.3, then 3.4 flags per 100 shifts over the four weeks from Sep 21 [table:v_qc_weekly]
- Harbor: 6.2 last week to 1.4 this week, the biggest improvement (12.2 in the week of Sep 21) [table:v_qc_weekly]
- Northside: 3 last week to 1.3 this week [table:v_qc_weekly]

x04:
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock; a shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart.
- Threshold: 10 or more consecutive knocks under 30 seconds apart [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back, so those knocks no longer count as doors or contacts; a whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full [doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
- Rolled-back knocks stay in the data marked rolled back, and rollbacks never change a client report already sent [doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
- An open flag needs a conversation with the field lead before the canvasser's next shift; two or more in one week go to the field director [doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
